description: chat.rs, contact.rs, message.rs, position.rs, presence.rs /set handlers extract the update map via args.as_object_mut().and_then(|m| m.remove("update")), which requires args to stay typed as Value throughout the function. The identity.rs fix correctly destructures Value::Object(mut args_map) at function entry and calls args_map.remove("update") directly — no as_object_mut() indirection. A serious Rust practitioner would prefer the destructuring form: it removes the Option layering, communicates that args is always an Object (which is true at the dispatch level), and makes every subsequent args.get/remove call one level cleaner. The current chat-handler form was chosen to avoid refactoring extract_account_id, which takes &Value — but once destructured, extract_account_id can receive &Value::Object(&args_map) or the function can be updated. As written, it is a borrow-checker workaround disguised as a method chain.
title: chat-server /set handlers: as_object_mut().and_then() for update-map removal
